title: CPU baseline matmul throughput
status: Measured on DE1-SoC · ARM Cortex-A9 · 2 threads, NEON SIMD kernel, 32×32 tiling
description:
CPU baseline for an N×N int8 matmul, measured with matmul_baseline_mt (tile 32, 2 threads, NEON kernel) on the DE1-SoC's dual-core ARM Cortex-A9. The linked text file has the raw output, every number and the full calculation.

Optimization setup:
- Tiling: 32×32 tiles.
- 2 threads: one per Cortex-A9 core. The rows of C are split between the threads, which never need to synchronise.
- SIMD NEON kernel: NEON instructions process 16 int8 values per 128-bit register. The kernel computes 4 output columns at once with 4 independent accumulators.
- Compiled with gcc -O3 -mcpu=cortex-a9 -mfpu=neon.

How GOP/s is calculated: GOP/s = 2 × N³ / time.
- An N×N by N×N matmul has N² outputs, and each output is a dot product of length N, so it does N³ multiply-accumulates (MACs).
- Each MAC counts as 2 operations (one multiply and one add), so the total is 2 × N³ operations.
- Dividing by the measured time in seconds gives operations per second; dividing by 10⁹ gives GOP/s.
- Example, N = 128: 2 × 128³ = 4,194,304 operations in 689.52 µs = 4,194,304 / 0.00068952 s = 6.083 × 10⁹ operations per second = 6.083 GOP/s.
